chunks: Sahl ibn Ziyad from Ibn Mahbub from Ibn Ri'ab from Zurarah from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him)
Regarding a man who bequeathed one-third of his wealth to his paternal uncles and maternal uncles, he said: 'To his paternal uncles two-thirds and to his maternal uncles one-third.'
23 - Sahl ibn Ziyad said: I wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him)

A man had two sons, one of whom died, and he had male and female offspring. Their grandfather bequeathed to them the share of their father. Is this share equal for male and female, or 'for the male the share of two females'? He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'They execute their grandfather's bequest as he ordered, if God wills.'

And I wrote to him: A man has male and female offspring, and he acknowledged for them a property that it is for his children, and did not mention that it is divided among them according to God's shares and prescriptions, where male and female are equal. He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'They execute in it their father's bequest as he specified. If he did not specify anything, they return it to the Book of God, if God wills.'
24 - And - Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar wrote to Abu Muhammad (peace be upon him)

A man bequeathed one-third of his wealth to his male and female freedmen. Is the male and female equal in it, or 'for the male the share of two females' from the bequest? He (peace be upon him) wrote: 'It is valid for the deceased to bequeath as he bequeathed, as he bequeathed, if God wills.'
ai.seo_question: How is the one-third bequest distributed among male and female relatives in Shia law?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the juristic principle that the testator’s explicit instruction in the one-third bequest (*wasiyyah*) takes precedence over default inheritance ratios, allowing for equal distribution among males and females if specified. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and Imam al-Rida (AS) confirm that executors must implement the deceased's precise wording, reverting to Quranic shares only if the bequest remains ambiguous or unspecified. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the autonomy of the testator within the legal boundaries of the one-third limit.
